transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah (Redwood); Rachel Owens, Daniel Cruz, Maya Li, Samir Patel (Meridian)

Summary: Procurement/legal focused call — go through MSA/DPA items Meridian flagged, confirm SLAs, and outline pilot/onboarding next steps.

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood here, I'll kick off. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Rachel Owens: Good thanks. We have a short agenda, legal team has redlines for both the MSA and the DPA, and procurement wants pricing clarity.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Great. We'll go section by section; Alex will cover commercial and onboarding, I can dive into security/architecture as needed.
[00:31] Maya Li: Quick ask up front — timeline wise we need vendor approval by mid-December to hit our Q1 rollout, so any delays in legal will push that.
[00:40] Alex Kim: Understood, timeline is tight. We think a short reserved-capacity pilot will help unblock procurement while legal finalizes terms.
[00:52] Daniel Cruz: On the DPA we've flagged data residency, encryption, and subprocessors. Can you confirm which regions data can be pinned to and where logs are stored?
[01:05] Priya Shah: Sure. For Redwood Hosted we have region pinning in our control plane; for Private and Dedicated we can restrict VPCs and self-hosted control plane so logs and data stay in your account. We support AES-256 at rest and KMS integration for key management.
[01:28] Samir Patel: Wait, KMS integration — is that customer-managed keys or only Redwood-managed?
[01:35] Priya Shah: We offer both. For Private deployments and Dedicated with enterprise add-on you can bring your own keys (KMS/HSM). On hosted we also have a customer-key option via an HSM-backed KMS integration.
[01:48] Rachel Owens: We'll need explicit contract language for BYOK and for audit access to key rotation logs. That was one of our redlines.
[02:00] Alex Kim: Noted. We can add a clause referencing KMS integration and audit log access. We'll propose specific wording in the redlined MSA.
[02:10] Maya Li: Pricing — your commercial team gave us three options. Can you confirm a committed capacity discount and how early termination looks?
[02:22] Alex Kim: Yes. High level: hosted is pay-as-you-go; dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with monthly commit tiers. Early termination is negotiable — typically we have a pro-rated termination fee for reserved contracts, but we'll show the exact language in the MSA.
[02:36] Daniel Cruz: SLA questions: We need 99.9% uptime at a min for inference endpoints and P95 latency guarantees for our internal SLAs. Is that in scope?
[02:48] Priya Shah: Our Dedicated product can support 99.9% SLA with routing and redundancy; for latency we publish performance profiles per model and we can set p95 latency targets in the SLA, though guaranteed latency depends on the model and sequence length. We do automatic fallback to lower-cost variants only with your consent.
[03:12] Rachel Owens: Also want to ensure there's a remediation credit schedule in case of SLA breaches.
[03:20] Alex Kim: Absolutely — standard SLA credits apply and we'll include a tiered credit schedule in the MSA.
[03:28] Maya Li: On subprocessors we need a list and a commitment to notify us of changes.
[03:34] Priya Shah: We'll share our subprocessors list and commit to 30-day notice for material changes.
[03:40] 
[03:45] - Transcript glitch / crosstalk -
[03:52] Daniel Cruz: There's some occlusion on my line, sorry.
[03:56] Priya Shah: No worries. Back to security docs — we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001; I'll upload certs and the security package link after the call.
[04:06] Rachel Owens: Please include pen-test report and a summary of your internal change control for models and quantization changes. We flagged model-change notification in the DPA.
[04:20] Priya Shah: We can provide change control docs and an alerting approach for model/regression changes. Redwood Optimize has monitoring for quality regressions tied to evals — we can include the workflow.
[04:36] Samir Patel: For onboarding, what's required from our SRE side? VPC peering? SAML?
[04:44] Alex Kim: For Private/Dedicated we do VPC peering or private link depending on cloud. SSO is SAML 2.0; we support SCIM provisioning and RBAC. For the pilot we'll provide a runbook with minimal networking: VPN or private link, service account, and sample workload.
[05:01] Maya Li: Can you share a sample runbook and the pilot success criteria? Procurement wants clear exit criteria.
[05:11] Miguel Torres: (Redwood CSM) We'll draft a pilot runbook with onboarding steps, success metrics (p95 latency <= X, throughput target Y, no data retention beyond KV cache TTL), and acceptance tests. We'll propose a 2-week pilot.
[05:28] Rachel Owens: That sounds reasonable. Legal also wants indemnification language clarified on data mishandling.
[05:36] Alex Kim: We'll provide the standard indemnification language and note where we can discuss carve-outs; we'll flag any concerns in the redline.
[05:44] Daniel Cruz: One more technical: you mentioned automatic prefix/KV caching — does that persist PII? We need guarantees that cache is ephemeral and can be wiped on demand.
[05:58] Priya Shah: Caching is configurable; KV caches are per-tenant and TTL-based. For Dedicated/Private you can set shorter TTLs and we expose cache flush APIs. We'll add explicit DPA language about cache persistence and deletion.
[06:15] Maya Li: Who signs the MSA on Redwood's side? Procurement wants to know contact and authority.
[06:22] Alex Kim: For commercial terms signature is by Redwood's VP of Commercial or authorized signatory; I'll include contact details in the packet.
[06:28] Rachel Owens: Great. On data residency again — can you guarantee that logs and raw transcripts from inference won't leave specified regions?
[06:38] Priya Shah: For Hosted we can pin region for storage, and for Dedicated/Private they remain in the customer's VPC or cloud account depending on deployment. We'll include language guaranteeing region residency for customer data and logs in the DPA.
[06:54] 
[07:00] Maya Li: Any known integrations with our existing KMS vendor — we use Azure Key Vault primarily.
[07:07] Priya Shah: We integrate with Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, and GCP KMS; HSM options available for Dedicated.
[07:15] Samir Patel: Ok. Back on pricing — we need the committed capacity pricing and also an estimate of per-token cost delta between hosted and dedicated.
[07:24] Alex Kim: We'll put exact numbers in the pricing sheet, but typically dedicated committed capacity reduces per-token unit cost by 30-45% depending on utilization and batching. We'll show a model comparing typical load patterns.
[07:40] Rachel Owens: Procurement also needs to confirm vendor onboarding docs and who will do background checks if required.
[07:47] Miguel Torres: We'll provide a vendor onboarding packet with references, SOC2 report, org chart, and point of contact for background checks.
[07:57] Daniel Cruz: A small point: will you allow us to have read-only access to audit logs for a rolling 12 months?
[08:06] Priya Shah: Yes, we can provide read-only audit log access; retention period can be negotiated — we typically offer 12 months but can extend as an add-on.
[08:17] Rachel Owens: Great. If you can get these items in a package next week, legal can review quickly.
[08:25] Alex Kim: We'll aim to have the redline and security package by 2025-11-20 and MSA redline by 2025-11-25.
[08:33] 
[08:36] - Background notes and small clarifications -
[08:40] Maya Li: One more question about fallback policies — if a model variant is deprecated, how will you handle compatibility for our production calls?
[08:49] Priya Shah: We have a deprecation policy with advance notice and automatic routing to compatible variants; for Dedicated we can keep pinned versions for a period. We'll include deprecation SLA in the docs.
[09:02] 
[09:05] Miguel Torres: Quick recap: items we'll deliver — redlined MSA and DPA, security package (SOC2/ISO/pen test), pilot runbook and benchmark template, pricing sheet for hosted vs dedicated, subprocessors list, and region residency confirmation.
[09:20] Rachel Owens: Thanks. If we can get that packet next week we'll move forward.
[09:25] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links.
[09:31] -- End of recording --

Recap (verbatim notes):
- Legal redlines: MSA + DPA (data residency, BYOK, audit logs, indemnification, subprocessors notice)
- Security: Provide SOC2, ISO, pen-test summary, KMS/HSM integration details
- SLA: Dedicated can reach 99.9% SLA; include credit schedule and p95 latency targets for included models
- Pricing: Provide committed capacity tiers and per-token delta estimates; show early-termination language
- Onboarding: 2-week pilot runbook, sample acceptance tests, and required SRE tasks (VPC, SAML, SCIM)

End transcript.
